messages.subject: Re: datadr
messages.body_plain:
Yes - for a tutorial with some toy examples, please see:

http://tesseradata.github.io/docs-datadr/

For a better illustration of using the tools on more real-life problems, see here:

http://tesseradata.github.io/example-vast-challenge/

These docs are undergoing a lot of change right now, but they should be good for the most part.

Also, I am working on a quickstart script that quickly gives a feel for a few of the possible operations you can do.  Here's an example of some code to run:

# quick start for local usage of datadr / trelliscope

# install packages
library(devtools)
install_github("datar", "tesseradata")
install_github("trelliscope", "tesseradata")

library(datadr)
library(trelliscope)

# express barley data as a local "distributed data frame"
barleyDdf <- ddf(barley)

# divide the ddf by the variable "site"
bySite <- divide(barleyDdf, by = "site")

# look at the ddf object
bySite

# look at subsets of the ddf
bySite[[1]]
bySite[["site=Grand Rapids"]]

# compute mean yield for each subset and recombine with "rbind"
recombine(bySite,
   apply = function(x) mean(x$yield),
   combine = combRbind())

## make a simple trelliscope display on this division

# initialize visualization database (vdb) connection
vdbConn("vdb", autoYes = TRUE)

# simple dotplot panel function
pf <- function(x)
   dotplot(variety ~ yield, data = x)
# test it on a subset
pf(bySite[[1]][[2]])

# simple cognostics function
cf <- function(x) {
   list(
      meanYield = cogMean(x$yield, desc = "mean yield"),
      range = cogRange(x$yield, desc = "yield range"),
      min = cog(min(x$yield), desc = "min yield"),
      max = cog(max(x$yield), desc = "min yield")
   )
}
# test it on a subset
cf(bySite[[1]][[2]])

# add display with this panel and cognostics function to vdb
makeDisplay(bySite,
   name = "variety_vs_yield",
   desc = "test display with barley data",
   panelFn = pf, cogFn = cf,
   width = 400, height = 400,
   lims = list(x = "same", y = "free")
)

# view the display
view()

messages.subject: Error posting guidelines
messages.body_plain:
Since there are so many possible combinations of components in an analysis environment (operating system, R version, Hadoop distribution, R package versions, etc.), it is useful to have as much information about your environment as possible to get to the bottom of the error.  Please consider providing as much of the following as possible:
R version
Operating system and version
If using Hadoop:
Hadoop distribution / version
Does a non-RHIPE Hadoop job run (such as the wordcount example)
Results of sessionInfo() called from R
The result of calling traceback() after the error occurs
Code to reproduce the error
If possible to share, prior to running the code with the error, set `options(error = quote(dump.frames("testdump", TRUE)))` and send the resulting `testdump.rda` file

messages.subject: Install RHIPE on Mac OS X
messages.subject_clean: Install RHIPE on Mac OS X
messages.body_plain:
Hello All,

N00b Disclaimer: I've never used R and could completely doing things wrong.

I'm following along in the quickstart and encountered a problem installing Rhipe. I have install R (3.1.0) via HomeBrew in my Mac 10.9 system. When I do the commands:

    install.packages("devtools") # if not installed
    library(devtools)
    install_github("datadr", "tesseradata")
    install_github("trelliscope", "tesseradata")

I eventually receive the following warning:

    * DONE (trelliscope)
Warning message:
package ‘Rhipe’ is not available (for R version 3.1.0)

I am assuming this is harmless, but wanted to know for sure.

Thanks for your time!

-- Andy

More complete log at (I apologize this service did not have R highlighting and out of laziness I didn't seek one that does, also the output seems to have completely filled my history buffer so it is not quite complete): https://dpaste.de/OJH2

messages.subject: Re: Install RHIPE on Mac OS X
messages.subject_clean: Install RHIPE on Mac OS X
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andy,

Good call - trelliscope lists RHIPE as a "suggested" package, so R tries to install it when you install trelliscope.  RHIPE is not necessary unless using Hadoop as the back end.  The warning can be ignored.  We should make a note of that in the quick start.

We also should provide more detail for how to install RHIPE - R is looking on CRAN for the Rhipe package and can't find it - it needs to be installed from a separate location and it has other dependencies such as protobuf 2.4.1.

Ryan
